The cloak array is designed using a conformal array of radiating sources.
The target is a conductive, cylindrical object with a height of 753 mm and a radius of 101.5 mm.
The frequency of the incident wave used in the experiment is 1.2 GHz.
The ridged horn antenna is used to illuminate the target.
The cloak array consists of 15 elements with a spacing of 125.6 mm.
The Ansys HFSS model is used to simulate the fields and validate the cloak performance.
Perfectly Matched Layer (PML) absorptive boundary conditions are used in the HFSS model.
The average suppression of the bistatic RCS patterns for the individually fed Cloak ON case is 18.4 dB.
The average suppression of the bistatic RCS patterns for the column-fed Cloak ON case is 17 dB.
A 16-port Mini-Circuits ZC16PD-24-S+ splitter is used to operate the 16-channel system.
The Kikusui PMC18-2A DC power supply is used to bias the voltage-controlled attenuators and phase shifters.
A pair of MATLAB-controlled Measurement Computing USB-3105 data acquisition systems are used to collect the measurement data.
The anechoic chamber is used to reduce spurious reflections and improve the accuracy of the measurements.
The cloak array is designed to cancel out the scattered fields following target/wavefront interaction.
The experiment is conducted using a ridged horn antenna and a 3D printed target.
The cloak array is capable of hiding a conductive, cylindrical target in free-space conditions.
